## 498af9326ab9

**A498-1 — Reproduced canonical-fitting shortcut; generator coverage limitation, not a reference-label defect.** The wrong rule in `checks/audit/498af9326ab9/probe.py::restricted_union` runs shortest-path union after forbidding backward motion along the coordinate with the larger start-to-goal displacement. It fits **5/5 usable canonical pairs** and **40/40 unique generated inputs**: every one of the 10 general profiles at each of `None`, `easy`, `medium`, and `hard`, with seed `100 * band_index + profile_index`, sample index `17`, and explicit `scene_profile` override. The 40 exact configurations are in `cases.json`; these are individual grids, not lesson windows. No lesson-level witness claim is made.

The supported Racket `apply` command independently confirmed all 46 expected outputs (5 canonical, 40 generated, 1 handbuilt). Its final result, batch index 45, is a 9×9 single corridor whose only route from blue `(4,1)` to red `(4,7)` includes the leftward segment `(3,5)` to `(3,3)`. Racket recolors 19 zero cells; the wrong rule finds no route and leaves those 19 cells unchanged. Coordinates are zero-based. The compact input, actual Racket output, rival output, exact command, hashes, and differing coordinates are retained in [counterexample.json](checks/audit/498af9326ab9/counterexample.json); the source-bound runtime receipt is [racket.json](checks/audit/498af9326ab9/racket.json).

**Input validation and domain membership:** the witness passes `self_check` with `[]`, and `observe_overrides` reports `{"scene_profile":"twin_gates"}` because `_profile_for` categorizes every nonsolid wall arrangement that way. It satisfies the written shortest-path rule, but is **outside actual generator constructor support**: it is neither an exact public input, an empty scene, a solid rectangular block, nor the single vertical barrier with two symmetric gaps built by `_twin_gates`. This distinction is essential: the evidence does not show a wrong output on an emitted sample. It shows that the declared broad maze semantics admit a meaningful rival-discriminating case that current generation never supplies, while profile recovery accepts it under an inaccurate name.

**Source explanation:** empty scenes, single rectangular obstacles, and one-barrier/two-gap scenes all permit optimal paths that progress monotonically along the markers' major displacement axis. The five exact public scenes also have this property. The rival therefore remains consistent with these construction families. The 40-case measurement supports the source argument but is not an exhaustive seed test. No `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` or `LESSON_COMPETITORS` declarations exist in this target; the audit introduces this rival explicitly instead of claiming it is an existing declaration.

**Recommended follow-up:** add a small constructive family with alternating walls that forces backward movement along the major displacement axis, and retain this rival as an executable canonical-fitting teaching check. Give that topology its own recoverable profile or tighten `twin_gates` recognition to its documented geometry. The rule mirror and canonical Racket need no change based on this evidence. No target or shared source was edited.

**Checks and identity:** generator SHA-256 `f19086ed76a796847d938f1e6499dce712b233f42d9955d2758106abbbc8ff68`; normalized canonical program SHA-256 `067c9281e33eb2ef6dac33786b4265e55ba7a63acd09fbe80dc3ddf0f440363f` (declared/executed rule hash `067c9281e33e`); Racket receipt's raw rule text SHA-256 `c3b4b10e06b9807ad7f328e2b38b8ec53f7018de6e5d524729bbb343077bf88e`. All 46 inputs pass validation; Python expected output equals actual Racket on 46/46. See [verification.json](checks/audit/498af9326ab9/verification.json), [cases.json](checks/audit/498af9326ab9/cases.json), and [commands.json](checks/audit/498af9326ab9/commands.json). Checks used the unchanged final audit target. No full battery, huge sweep, or unrelated target inspection was performed.

## 498af9326ab9

**A1 — Reproduced directional support hole / plausible marker-order shortcut.**
The audited generator is unchanged at SHA-256
`f19086ed76a796847d938f1e6499dce712b233f42d9955d2758106abbbc8ff68`;
the selected rule hash is `067c9281e33e`.

Across 11,000 validator-accepted draws—6,000 exact profile×difficulty cases
(100 per each of 15 profiles in four bands) plus 5,000 default draws—every scene
placed blue weakly northwest of red: `start_row <= goal_row` and
`start_col <= goal_col`. No emitted scene reversed either semantic direction.
The generator therefore does not refute a brittle learner that applies the true
shortest-path-union computation only under that color/order convention.

The retained witness starts from an ordinary medium `open_rectangle` draw
(`seed=4982026`, `sample_index=17`) and swaps colors 1 and 2. The swapped 11×11
input still passes `self_check`, is still observed as `scene_profile=open_rectangle`,
and belongs to the generator's documented accepted profile domain, but is never
emitted by the sampler. The orientation-guarded rival returns the unchanged input
when blue is southeast of red; the selected Racket authority instead marks the
62-cell shortest-path union. `arcpuzzles apply` reports a valid output and binds
it to the audited generator and rule hashes.

Evidence: `checks/audit/498af9326ab9/evidence.json`, `input.json`, `racket.json`,
and reproducible `probe.py`. Reproduction from the packet root:

```text
python3 review.py run python3 ../checks/audit/498af9326ab9/probe.py
python3 review.py run python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 498af9326ab9 --input ../checks/audit/498af9326ab9/input.json --out ../checks/audit/498af9326ab9/racket.json
python3 review.py run python3 ../checks/audit/498af9326ab9/probe.py --racket ../checks/audit/498af9326ab9/racket.json
```

Suggested local repair: add an exact endpoint-order/orientation axis or apply a
color-preserving 180°/reflection transform after scene construction, and test all
four relative marker quadrants. No audit-target source was edited.
